passage.title: Bukhari and Muslim, from Ibn Umar
paras: Islam is built upon five: testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing the prayer, giving zakah, Hajj, and fasting Ramadan.

head: Pillar
Meaning
Key point
rows: Witnessing Allah's oneness and the Prophet's ﷺ message
Said with knowledge and acted on
At their times, with their conditions
Once in a lifetime if able

panels.title: Meaning of the shahadah
points: La ilaha illa Allah: none deserves worship but Allah
Muhammadur rasulullah: obey and follow him

questions.q: Explain the meaning of 'la ilaha illa Allah'.
questions.a: There is no one worthy of worship except Allah: it denies all false gods and affirms worship for Allah alone.

questions.q: How many pillars of Islam are there?
Memorise and write the hadith 'Islam is built upon five' in English (and Arabic if you can), then a pillar fact file on the pupil PDF: meaning, one ruling and one benefit for each pillar.
questions.a: Accurate hadith; fact file with meaning, ruling and benefit per pillar

questions.q: Extend: why is the shahadah first?
questions.a: Every act of worship rests on believing in Allah alone and following the Prophet ﷺ.

questions.q: Stretch: which pillar do you find hardest and how will you improve?
Which pillar is once in a lifetime for those able?
questions.a: A) Hajj. Hajj is required once for those able (3:97).

questions.q: Zakah on savings above nisab is ...
Think again: what does a missing pillar teach?
questions.a: Each pillar is essential; without one, a Muslim's practice is weakened.
